subject: Follow-up: CareBridge deployment options & compliance checklist
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emily Singh <emily.singh@carebridgehealth.org>, Alex Ortiz <a.ortiz@carebridgehealth.org>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up: deployment options & compliance checklist

Hi Emily / Alex —

Great to meet earlier — appreciate the time and the clear framing of CareBridge's requirements. Quick recap and the recommended next steps so we can align on the right deployment mode given your regulatory needs.

Key requirements you shared:
- HIPAA protected PHI in prompt/response flows
- Need for a signed BAA before any production data
- Quarterly security audits and audit-log access for internal compliance team
- Preference for in-region hosting (US) and data retention controls

Deployment options (short):
1) Hosted API (fastest onboarding) — supports encryption-in-transit and at-rest, and we can offer a BAA for many customers, but it relies on our multitenant hosted control plane. Good for low-friction pilots, less ideal if you need strict network isolation or on-prem audit controls.
2) Dedicated capacity — reserved GPU pools in a customer-dedicated tenancy. Predictable throughput, stronger isolation, and commonly chosen by customers who need an SLA + BAA and tighter operational boundaries.
3) Private (VPC / on-prem) — full network isolation, customer-managed VPC or on-prem bundle. Best for customers with stringent audit, data residency or air-gap needs.

Given CareBridge's requirement for quarterly audits and direct audit-log access, my recommendation is to evaluate Dedicated capacity as the primary path (predictable SLA + BAA + exportable logs). If your legal or InfoSec team requires host-level separation or on-prem evidence, we should scope Private (VPC or on-prem) — that will add lead time for provisioning.

Attachments I’m including: a draft BAA template, our latest SOC 2 snapshot, and a short security questionnaire we’d like you to complete so we can produce a tailored compliance pack.

Next steps I propose:
- You confirm whether CareBridge needs host-level isolation or if Dedicated meets the control set (reply to this thread)
- Dev / infra: estimated concurrent requests and average prompt size (tokens) — helps sizing for Dedicated
- I’ll share a ballpark pricing matrix for Dedicated vs Private and a procurement checklist
- If you prefer, we can do a 30-min follow-up with our security engineer (Laura) next week to walk through audit/log access and retention controls.

Available slots: Mon 2/23 10:00-11:30 PST or Tue 2/24 09:30-11:00 PST.

Thanks — looking forward to locking down the right path.

Regards,
Marcus Lin
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference

Thanks Marcus — helpful summary. A couple quick clarifications from our side: 

- SOC2 snapshot: is that the full report or an attestation summary? Our InfoSec team typically requires the SOC2 Type II attestation and the control matrix.
- Audit logs: can we pull logs (API) for a defined retention window (we anticipate 7 years for some records)?
- Does Redwood support an on-prem appliance or is 'Private' always a VPC-hosted control plane?

For the immediate next step, please send the ballpark numbers for Dedicated vs Private so procurement can start preliminary budgeting. Also yes — we'd like Laura on the follow-up call to discuss log access.

Emily

On Fri, Feb 20, 2026 at 10:03 AM Emily Singh <emily.singh@carebridgehealth.org> wrote:
> Thanks Marcus — helpful summary. A couple quick clarifications from our side: 
> 
> - SOC2 snapshot: is that the full report or an attestation summary? Our InfoSec team typically requires the SOC2 Type II attestation and the control matrix.
> - Audit logs: can we pull logs (API) for a defined retention window (we anticipate 7 years for some records)?
> - Does Redwood support an on-prem appliance or is 'Private' always a VPC-hosted control plane?

Thanks — quick answers below and I can have Laura expand on the controls in the call:

- SOC2: the attached "Redwood_SOC2_snapshot_2024.pdf" is an executive attestation summary plus the control mapping we share publicly. For customers that require a full SOC2 Type II report, we can provide an auditor access package under NDA; we typically coordinate that through our compliance team during contract negotiations.

- Audit logs: yes — we provide exportable audit logs and an API to pull request/response metadata and system events. For Dedicated deployments we can also enable a streaming export to your SIEM. Retention windows are configurable — 7 years is feasible but may have cost/archiving implications we can include in the quote.

- Private vs on-prem: our Private offering supports both a VPC-hosted private control plane (customer VPC peering) and a turnkey on-prem package for customers requiring physical network separation. On-prem requires additional lead time and an on-site install plan; we’ll include high-level timelines in the procurement checklist.

I’ll attach a short procurement checklist and ballpark pricing for Dedicated and Private options tomorrow (Mon). In the meantime, could you confirm: expected monthly token volume and peak concurrent requests (approx)? That will materially affect the Dedicated sizing.

Laura — are you available Mon 2/23 10:00 PST to join a 30-min call?

— Marcus
From: Alex Ortiz <a.ortiz@carebridgehealth.org>

Marcus / Emily — thanks for the clarity. From procurement's point of view: 

- We need ballpark TCV and monthly run-rate for Dedicated vs Private (total cost over 12 months) so we can include in the fiscal Q2 budget.
- Lead time is important — can you indicate expected lead time for Dedicated (provisioning + BAA in place) vs Private on-prem?

We’re leaning to start with Dedicated capacity if the BAA + log export meets InfoSec requirements, then revisit Private if we need host-level separation next year.

Please send the pricing + procurement checklist and I’ll route to our procurement tech lead. Also copying procurement@carebridgehealth.org so they have the thread.

Alex Ortiz

CareBridge Health
